name: Hanyang CRR
full_name: Hanyang/Yonsei master-slave catheter-guidewire driving systems (assembly-type 2016; coaxial controller-responder robot CRR 2023)
group: Hanyang University (Byung-Ju Yi) with Yonsei University Severance Hospital (Jong Yun Won)
versions: cha2016_assembly (Proc IMechE H 231(1):69-79, issue 2017, online 2016: assembly-type 4-DOF master-slave, phantom) -> Woo 2019 Appl Sci (5-DOF, haptic) and Song 2021 Appl Sci (in vivo usability), cited by kim2023 refs 14-15, not read -> 2022 its 5-DOF slave used as the guidewire/guide-catheter advancer of DGIST's ECMIS, 2 swine (hwang2022_ecmis p. 8) -> kim2023_robotassisted (JVIR 2023: 7-DOF coaxial controller-responder robot, CRR, human pilot)
target_anatomy: hepatic arteries for TACE (CRR); arterial phantom (2016)
devices_driven: 2016: 5 F catheter and 0.035-in guidewire (cha2016_assembly p. 75); CRR: 5 F catheter, 0.035-in guidewire, 2.2 F microcatheter (Progreat) and 0.014-in micro-guidewire (Meister), 4 devices (kim2023_robotassisted p. 1566-1567); how many move simultaneously N.R.
n_dof_detail: 4 (2016: insertion and rotation of catheter and guidewire, cha2016_assembly p. 71); 7 (CRR: insertion and rotation of catheter, guidewire and micro-guidewire, insertion of microcatheter, kim2023_robotassisted p. 1566)
translation_detail: friction-roller (2016 guidewire: active and passive roller, spring-adjusted friction) plus other: rack-and-pinion carriage that moves the catheter drive (cha2016_assembly p. 72); CRR drive type N.R. (kim2023_robotassisted)
rotation_detail: 2016: plastic gear trains rotate the catheter (Y-connector fixed to the rotation part) and the guidewire roller unit (cha2016_assembly p. 72); CRR N.R.
device_range: commercially available devices; 2016 catheter drive stroke 460 mm (cha2016_assembly p. 73); CRR 5 F catheter stroke 45 cm, microcatheter stroke 20 cm longer (kim2023_robotassisted p. 1568-1569)
force_sensing: Guidewire-tip contact estimated from actuator current, no dedicated sensor: under 200 mA in a straight artery, +300 mA curved, +500 mA blocked (cha2016_assembly p. 76); CRR N.R.
haptics_leader: 2016: 2-DOF parallel-mechanism master (insertion, rotation) with two DC motors for haptic feedback, activate/release and catheter/guidewire mode buttons (cha2016_assembly p. 74); CRR: finger-grip handle with activate/release buttons (kim2023_robotassisted p. 1566), force feedback N.R.
imaging_compat: 2016: camera over a transparent water-filled phantom; CRR: hybrid angio-CT suite (Canon INFX-8000C with Aquilion), robot mounted on the angiotable (kim2023_robotassisted p. 1567, Fig. 2a)
sterility: Device-contacting parts detach and are EtO-sterilised (all but the roller actuator part), assembly 86 s (cha2016_assembly p. 73, 77); the same for the CRR (kim2023_robotassisted citing cha2016)
validation_detail: 2016: bench (10 insertion trials) and phantom (4 users x 3 trials; survey of 8) (cha2016_assembly); 2022: 2 swine as ECMIS advancer (hwang2022_ecmis); kim2023: single-centre prospective pilot, 10 HCC patients, 5 robot-assisted vs 5 conventional TACE, one operator; technical success 4/5 patients and 7/8 target vessels (one failure: 5 F catheter twisted in the telescope); no procedure-related adverse event
key_numbers: 2016: max insertion error 0.63 mm, max response time 16 ms (cha2016_assembly). CRR: operator dose median 0.4 vs 53.2 uSv (P = .005); patient dose 2,167.5 vs 2,989.7 uSv (P = .311); procedure time median 56 (47-65) vs 37 (30-58) min (P = .101); 8 of 30 TACE steps robotised (abstract; Results: 8 of 22 procedural steps) (kim2023_robotassisted)
